#4913. Segway launches the $1,999 Xyber Air, bringing its futuristic moped-style e-bike to the masses

When Segway launched the original Xyber last year, it was one of those e-bikes that immediately turned heads. With its futuristic styling, oversized frame, and high-performance off-road ambitions, it looked more like a concept vehicle than something you could actually buy.

Now the company is hoping to capture a much wider audience with the new Segway Xyber Air, a lighter, street-legal version that keeps much of the original’s aggressive styling while fitting neatly into the familiar Class 1, 2, and 3 e-bike categories.

At first glance, you’d be forgiven for mistaking the Xyber Air for its larger sibling. It retains the angular frame design and moto-inspired proportions that made the original stand out, complete with Segway’s signature X-shaped front and rear lighting.

But beneath the familiar styling is a much more approachable machine.

Power comes from a 750W nominal rear hub motor producing 80 Nm of torque, with peak output reaching 1,600W.

Riders can choose between Class 1, Class 2, and Class 3 operation depending on local regulations, with speeds of up to 20 mph (32 km/h) in Class 1 and 2 modes or 28 mph (45 km/h) in Class 3.

Segway has even included a Hybrid Mode that allows throttle operation up to 20 mph while pedal assist continues to 28 mph without requiring riders to switch between ride modes.

That’s still kosher in many states, but some are starting to require true Class 3 e-bikes to have no throttle operation at all, so check your local regulations to make sure you’re compliant.

The bike is powered by a 717 Wh battery that Segway claims can deliver up to 58 miles (93 km) of range, though as always, real-world mileage will depend heavily on rider weight, terrain, and how enthusiastically that throttle gets used.

Suspension duties are handled by an 80 mm dual-crown front fork, paired with 20×4-inch fat tires and hydraulic disc brakes with 180 mm rotors.

The bike also borrows several features more commonly associated with motorcycles, including traction control, hill-start assist, regenerative hill descent control, and automatic lighting.

Whether or not an e-bike requires traction control or hill hold remains to be seen, but it’s neat to know that such moto-inspired tech is heading into the e-bike space.

Segway continues to lean heavily into connected features as well. The Xyber Air includes AirLock automatic unlocking, Apple Find My compatibility, GPS tracking, Lost Mode remote disabling, over-the-air updates, and a full-color TFT display with navigation and smartphone integration.

Some connected services will require a subscription after the first year, which is unfortunately becoming a trend in the micromobility world, but makes sense given the data connection required for those services. Still, it’d be nice to see more of a grace period, like two to three years, for connected features, since it’s not like we’re downloading gigabyte-heavy movies on our bikes.

Despite all of those features, components, and tech, the Xyber Air weighs a claimed 84 lb (38 kg), which is noticeably lighter than the original Xyber, while still supporting a 330 lb (150 kg) payload. It’s also UL 2271 and UL 2849 certified.

Sure, 84 pounds is a lot of poundage for an e-bike, but compared to the moto-styled original, it’s on a significant diet.

Ordering will open on October 27 at a launch price of $1,999, though customers can already sign up on the sales page to get availability notifications.

I actually think Segway made the right move here.

The original Xyber had that cool flair to it, but it also blurred the line between e-bike and electric motorcycle, or shot right past it in many places. The Xyber Air looks like Segway took a step back and asked, “What if we kept the styling that people liked but made it fit within the existing e-bike framework?”

Basically, they kept the “Let’s take a shot at SUPER73” mindset but aimed for a more acceptable format considering today’s regulatory landscape.

The result is still unmistakably moto-inspired, but it’s also something that can legally access bike infrastructure in many places instead of existing in a regulatory gray area. At under $2,000, it also lands at a price point that opens the door to a larger audience.

It’s still not going to compete against the value proposition in something like the Juiced Scrambler, either in hardtail or full-suspension format, but it definitely looks like a fun ride. And with more options for more riders, there’s always going to be something for everyone!

#4912. 9 Decorative Plates for When You’re Sick of Boring Dishes (2026)

The great thing about decorative plates is that they don’t have to disappear into storage once dinner is over. Hang a few on a display wall, prop one up alongside your favorite cookbooks, or work it into a shelf vignette. So what makes one worth showing off? It’s the details that spark curiosity: A scalloped edge, an unexpected color combination, or a hand-painted pattern can be enough to make you look twice. “Any plate with a fun decorative motif, bright colors, or an interesting shape makes it more than just simply functional,” says Olympia Irving of Carolina Irving and Daughters.

Of course, good looks are only part of the appeal. The most memorable pieces often have a story to tell, whether it's a vintage find or a handmade design with charming, artisanal characteristics. Even the finish can make a statement. “I often find myself drawn to surfaces that look like they’re in flux—glazes that pool unpredictably or finishes that suggest movement or fragility, even in solid materials," says Anna Jewsbury, founder and artistic director of Completedworks.

There's no need to play by the rules of a perfectly coordinated table setting. A little contrast, a playful border, or a beautifully imperfect finish makes for a more interesting table—one that looks like it can only belong to you. Ahead, nine decorative plates that deserve a spot in your regular rotation and perhaps a prime position in your china cabinet.

For a plate that has lived a completely different life before landing on your table—try this Completedworks dinner plate made from recycled glass. Sculptural and subversive, it’s made from broken windows, melted glass bottles, and is repurposed using old engine oil as fuel. “We often play with the illusion of softness in materials that are anything but. Those moments where form and material are at odds are the ones I find most compelling,” Jewsbury shares.

Transport yourself to the French countryside with this Villeroy & Boch dinner plate. Part of the brand's beloved French Garden collection, its fruit-and-floral motif brings to mind sun-drenched afternoons and leisurely lunches in the garden. Even fruit and pastries straight from the market become a proper breakfast spread.

Does anything scream summer more than seashell-shaped splatterware? These Concha plates by editor-favorite brand Carolina Irving & Daughters bring together a seaside-inspired shape along with a creative, painterly glaze. “It is easy to make a table setting pop by only adding a few decorative touches, whether that is a dessert plate or a salt dish,” Irving says. “Truthfully, we love to use decorative plates as our everyday dishware!”

Designed by Cabana and made by heritage Italian porcelain house Ginori 1735, the painterly motif on this plate adds an element of rustic Italian charm to the table. Whether you stick to a cohesive set or play around with different colors and patterns for a more collected vibe, these plates can make even the simplest meals feel storied.

Score a vintage-inspired find without the hours spent scouring antique shops. Olive Ateliers did the legwork with its Vincent Plate, featuring a hand-painted floral motif, an aged blue rim, and an ivory ceramic base. “A plate becomes more when it holds history,” shares Laura Sotelo, cofounder of Olive Ateliers. “The wow isn’t about perfection—it’s about the story it carries. It should feel like it belonged somewhere long before it ended up in your hands.”

Each plate is finished by hand, giving it the character of a one-of-a-kind discovery. One important distinction: This plate isn't food-safe, so save it for a spot on your wall or shelf instead.

The soft pale yellow tones and the scalloped edge are some of our favorite details about these affordable, vintage-inspired dinner plates by West Elm. They are perfect for those who want to dip their toes into a decorative tabletop but aren’t quite ready to splurge. Sold in sets of four or eight, they strike the right balance between charm and accessibility and are ideal for daily use.

Your next dinner party can channel a little Italian holiday spirit with these hand-painted plates, crafted in a family-run workshop on the Amalfi Coast. They're available in two sizes, so they're equally charming piled high with antipasti or passed around the table with the main course.

A collaboration between L’Objet and South African artist Ruan Hoffmann, this plate brings a bold edge to the table with its painterly design and hand-applied 24k gold accents. While it’s smaller in dimension (6.5 inches), it makes a subtle statement and can complement your existing dinnerware.

If you're a fan of British artist Tess Newall's painterly work, you'll be happy to know her designs have made their way to the dinner table, courtesy of Porta. The “Ottoline” plates take inspiration from English country houses, Bloomsbury interiors, and traditional European ceramics. These hand-painted pieces are adorned with scrolling motifs, dotted edges, and wave detailing in contrasting shades of slate blue and rust. Sold in sets of four, they're a lovely way to bring a little art history to the table.

#4911. The 8 Best Slip-On Walking Shoes, According to Our Editors

Looking to get out the door quicker? Don’t let laces slip you up.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SLIDING INTO A pair of slip-on walking shoes might be the easiest thing you’ll do all day. This footwear was built for speed and convenience, making it an accessory that deserves valuable real estate by your door.

Slip-on walking shoes have a rocky history—older versions had a looser fit, raising the risk of instability and friction, especially with higher mileage. But newer designs use no-tie laces, sock liners, pull tabs, and collapsible heels to create a custom fit that rivals what you’ll get with traditional laces.

These shoes are an obvious choice if you have dexterity issues, but they're also just convenient for everyone looking for an easy pair of walking shoes. Slip-on walking shoes also offer more structure than other laceless shoe designs, which has earned them a fanbase with podiatrists. “They are typically a much better option than flip-flops or slides because they provide more stability and keep the foot properly secured,” says Melissa Lockwood, DPM, a podiatrist at Heartland Foot and Ankle Associates in Bloomington, Illinois.

Nicole Graf, DPM, founder of Lexington Podiatry and associate professor at the University of Kentucky, also calls slip-on walking shoes a “huge step up” from flip-flops and slides.

Slip-on walking shoes aren’t for everyone. The fit can still throw some people off, and some simply prefer the tighter feel that laces deliver. But if you want travel-friendly shoes you can toss on in a second, these are a solid choice. As people who value quality, supportive footwear, Men’s Health editors have put in plenty of miles in slip-on walking shoes. The below check all the boxes.

The On Cloud 6 is an excellent example of how good a slip-on shoe can be. You can get in and out of this sneaker with no issue thanks to its wide opening, but the shoe’s elastic “speed” laces and sockliner create a snug fit once you’re in. (Those elastic laces can be adjusted to find your perfect fit.)

The sneaker uses Zero-Gravity CloudTec, which is On’s signature lightweight foam with hollow pods below for a cushioned, yet stable, feel underfoot. (Just be aware that those pods are prone to trapping small pebbles and debris.) A built-in flexible plate, called a Speedboard, helps push you forward with each step. This shoe also comes in a waterproof option, if you’re into rainy strolls. With a wide range of color options and an unobnoxious design, you can pair these with just about anything.

It’s tough to find a quality shoe under $100 right now, let alone one from a big brand. But the Adidas Cloudfoam Cuxxion Sock Shoes have some colorways under $50, making them an ideal choice for budget shoppers who don’t want to mess with laces.

This shoe uses Adidas’ signature Cloudfoam technology at the midsole for a plush, cushioned feel. Its Adiwear outsole is durable and grippy enough for most needs, too. But the real standout in this shoe is its elastic sock upper. It molds to your foot to create a surprisingly snug feel, even for narrow feet. The elastic sock collar supports that secure feel, although it may be too tight for people with wider ankles. The engineered knit upper is highly breathable, lowering the odds you’ll end your walk with sweaty feet. We appreciate the oversized pull tabs in front and back, making the process of getting these on and off seamless.

Feet come in all sizes, making it tough to find a slip-on shoe that works for everyone—and putting adjustable features at a premium. The Nike Pegasus 42 EasyOn has a specialized EasyOn lacing and bungee system up top to help you get the level of tightness you want, before locking it into place. (The lock and bungee combination takes some practice to get right at first.)

The shoe has a collapsible heel that springs back into place once you’re in, making the process of getting these on seamless. It’s also crafted with the same ReactX foam and Air Zoom unit as the standard—and popular—Nike Pegasus 42 running shoe, delivering an energetic feel under your feet. Convenient pull tabs at the heel sit flush against the shoe when they’re not in use, adding to the shoe’s overall sleekness.

Read More: Best Walking Shoes for Men Over 50

Stability shoes are designed to guide your foot with each step and prevent too much inward rolling as you go. But choosing a stability shoe usually means sacrificing a high level of cushioning, since a shoe that feels too plush may not be overly supportive. Hoka’s Skyward Laceless manages to create a stable, locked-in feel while still delivering plenty of the brand’s signature cushioning underfoot.

The Skyward Laceless has a stretchy upper that gently hugs your foot, creating a sock-like feel. The ankle and instep are equally snug, which can be a good or bad thing, depending on your foot size and width. This shoe has plenty of foam below for a slightly bouncy feel, but it still corrects your stride as you go. The integrated tongue pull tab is a nice touch, making for easier entry.

The Under Armour SlipSpeed Mega is packed with features you won’t find in most slip-on walking shoes, creating a versatile, unique sneaker. For starters, this shoe converts from a sneaker design to a recovery slipper with the help of a collapsible heel. (Under Armour refers to this as going from “speed mode” to “slip mode.”)

The shoe skips elastic laces or a sockliner upper in favor of Under Armour’s specialized BOA fit system, a 12-point dial that you can turn to adjust the width across the midfoot. The wide base creates a stable feel, while lots of foam cushioning underfoot delivers a plushness you’ll appreciate. A heads-up: This shoe is slightly heavier than others at 11.7 ounces. That’s a difference you may start to feel on long walks.

After a grueling workout, it feels borderline pampering to slide into the right recovery shoe. The Kane Footwear Active Recovery Shoe is armed with features that should make it a fixture in your gym bag.

This slip-on has strong arch support and a slight rocker shape to help ease pressure on the bottom of your feet as you walk. Internal nodes in the footbed help to promote blood flow and circulation down below, while the shoe’s surprisingly secure design helps prevent slipping. The Active Recovery Shoe is water-resistant with an airy design that allows you to take this in and out of the gym shower without ending up with sopping feet. Heel tabs in back make it simple to get in and out.

Merrell is known for its rugged, outdoor footwear and hiking shoes. While the Merrell Jungle Moc isn’t exactly a hiking shoe, it’s a solid option when you want good traction, whether you’re navigating rocky ground or a slippery surface. The Jungle Moc has been a bestseller for years, with its simple slip-on design and high level of cushioning.

Dual side stretch panels and an exaggerated heel tab make it simple to get in and out of these shoes. The suede upper is breathable, but water-resistant to keep you dry in nearly all conditions. The Jungle Moc has a cushioned EVA midsole for stability and comfort, too. While these shoes are easy to get on, the curved heel makes it harder to slide out—just something to be aware of.

Clogs admittedly aren’t the right style for everyone—some offer less support than sneakers and may slip around more than a standard shoe. But the sleek Crocs Dylan Clog is a solid option for people who want a clog style without some of the common issues that come with it.

The Dylan Clog has a deep heel cup to help lock your foot in, lowering the risk it’ll move around as you step. It’s also made from one piece of Croslite (Crocs’ signature material) to prevent wear and tear over time. This shoe looks like leather thanks to its subtle pebbled texture, but it’s water-resistant and dries quickly when wet. The only major downside is that it’s not very breathable in front. If you’re prone to sweaty toes, this may not be the shoe for you.

Not all shoes are created equal, but the best slip-on walking shoes have all of the supportive features you’ll find in standard lace-up walking shoes. “You mostly get what you pay for in these,” says Richard H. Graves, DPM, a podiatrist at Sol Foot & Ankle Centers in Long Beach, California. He suggests taking a pass at dirt-cheap slip-on walking shoes. “The cheaper ones are not going to provide enough support in the long run, even if they might feel good at first,” Graves says. “There should be enough structure to support your arch and the midsole should be firm and not too flimsy.”

Many high-quality slip-on walking shoes provide similar comfort to regular sneakers. Look for elements like a breathable upper, pull tabs to make them easy to get on and off, and a roomy toe box. Structured heel panels and extra padding in this area help to keep your foot secure, even without standard laces.

Traction for slip-on walking shoes will vary depending on the type of shoe you choose. Most will offer decent traction—meaning, enough so you don’t feel like you’re slipping on wet or damp pavement. But a more rugged shoe like the Merrell Jungle Moc has a grippier sole to help provide extra traction over rockier ground.

Yes, slip-on walking shoes can provide arch support. If this is an important quality for you, look for features like contoured footbeds and a stable midsole. You’ll also want a shoe that fits well and stays put once it’s on to ensure your arch support is consistent. “Make sure that you're not getting them too loose just to make it easier to slide on and off—then you'll be sacrificing support,” Graves says.

To find the best men’s slip-on walking shoes, MH editors tested the most recent and popular pairs on the market, evaluating each for support, comfort, and traction. Because these shoes are designed for walking, not just comfort, durability was also a key factor. To round things out, we consulted three podiatrists for their input on how to evaluate a slip-on walking shoe, along with the value of this style. Based on their advice and our experience, we chose these slip-on walking shoes.

#4910. LiveWire set to show off several new electric motorcycles next month

LiveWire is preparing to bring its biggest electric two-wheeler lineup yet to EICMA (Milan Motorcycle Show) next month, including a pair of previously unseen models that will offer a preview of where the electric motorcycle company is headed in 2027.

The company will exhibit alongside its majority shareholder Harley-Davidson at the massive Milan motorcycle show, running November 5-8, where its booth will span everything from STACYC electric balance bikes to the lightweight S4 Honcho platform and the more performance-oriented DUST family.

Perhaps the biggest surprise will be the first public appearance of the new S4 Honcho Skate. LiveWire hasn’t revealed much about the bike yet, other than confirming it will expand the Honcho family when it arrives in 2027. We won’t have to wait until EICMA for all the details, though, as LiveWire says preliminary specs and additional information will be released on November 2.

The Skate will join the S4 Honcho Street and S4 Honcho Trail, giving LiveWire a growing family of lightweight electric motorcycles built around its modular S4 platform. The production-ready Honcho Street will also make its European debut at EICMA before going on sale there immediately after the show. Its U.S. launch is scheduled for next week.

LiveWire is also continuing to flesh out its newly acquired DUST lineup. After acquiring the assets of Dust Moto earlier this year, LiveWire will show off a production-intent version of the DUST Hightail, which is targeting a 2027 introduction.

Alongside it will be another new model known as the DUST Spur, also planned for 2027. Like the Honcho Skate, details remain thin for now, with preliminary specifications coming November 2 and final production specs and pricing expected in the first quarter of next year.

The expanding lineup is particularly interesting because it shows just how far LiveWire is moving beyond the premium full-size electric motorcycles that defined the brand’s early years.

Between STACYC, the lightweight Honcho models, and the more dirt-focused DUST machines, LiveWire is increasingly building a ladder of electric two-wheelers aimed at riders across a much wider range of ages, experience levels, and budgets.

We’ll get a much better look at the newest rungs on that ladder in just a couple of weeks.

#4909. Construction Carnaval: electric equipment comes to Brazil with SDLG

SDLG Brasil has completed its first sale in the South American country, delivering an order of six heavy-duty electric wheel loaders to Brazilian mining, construction, and infrastructure company Grupo Base.

Grupo Base ordered four, 27-ton L972 HEV and a pair of, 12.5-ton L938 HEV loaders from Chinese equipment brand Shandong Lingong Construction Machinery Co., Ltd. (the “SD” is “ShanDong,” the LG is “LinGong”) back in June, and the first of the machines are now reportedly on-site, moving dirt, but not making noise.

“This contract is a historic milestone and comes at a time when we have taken on commercial responsibility for SDLG across 60% of Brazil,” says Carlos Renato Machado, executive director of SDLG’s Brazilian distributor, Tracbel, before adding that the company hoped to expand the use of electric mining and construction equipment throughout the region.

The SDLG machines draw power from 423 and 180 kWh LFP battery packs, respectively, with the larger machines sending power to a 230 kW (~305 hp) electric motor and the smaller machines getting a 180 kW (~240 hp) one. Both specs promise a full day’s worth of continuous operation and fast DC charging between shifts.

Grupo Base operates a fleet of 450 heavy equipment assets at more than 30 concrete and mortar batching plants and 20 crushed stone and fracking sand sites, employing more 2,000 people. The electrification of those assets would represent a massive environmental benefit to the ecologically sensitive region – and that’s a fact not lost on Grupo Base executives.

“We are driving a major transformation across our operations,” says Edson Pechio, president and CEO of Grupo Base, said. “We want to incorporate solutions that will enable us to operate more efficiently and progressively reduce greenhouse gas emissions.”

#4908. Where Does Mark Ruffalo Live? Exploring the Avengers Star’s East Coast Real Estate Portfolio

He’s currently booked and busy, but where does Mark Ruffalo live when he’s not filming? The Oscar-nominated actor appears in five projects released in 2026 alone. With that kind of schedule, the Marvel star must maintain somewhat of a nomadic lifestyle. It’s no surprise that, for years, he and his family juggled properties on both coasts. These days, however, Ruffalo is all in on New York—when he isn’t traveling to movie sets around the world.

Read on to learn more about the Emmy winner’s homes in the Big Apple and beyond.

Ruffalo first visited the small town of Callicoon in New York’s Catskills region in the mid-’90s, according to a December 2017 interview with Men’s Journal. Soon after visiting Callicoon, the 28-year-old Ruffalo paid $63,000 for his first home there: a 27-acre property with a one-room cabin. Around 2001, he and his wife, Sunrise Coigney, purchased an estate there, on a former dairy farm, complete with a 19th-century post-and-beam barn. “Smartest thing I ever did,” the Avengers star told the outlet. “It ended up having a huge influence on my life in many ways.”

At first, Ruffalo and his family split their time between their Los Angeles and New York homes. But that soon began to wear on the couple, spurring the decision to sell their Hollywood Hills property in 2009 and move to Callicoon full-time. “The whole guiding idea for living upstate was to simplify,” Ruffalo said in 2011. “It’s the best thing I could have done for the family as a whole and for the kids in particular.… We’re letting them grow a little wild, and we step in when it’s essential, but in a lot of ways they figure stuff out on their own and they do it in a way that’s organic and lasts. We live in a small space and we’re really influenced by the natural world around us. Eventually that is reflected in one’s behavior and how you get along with other people. There’s a lot of quiet in the country and there’s a lot of quietness in my children.”

On the farm, the Now You See Me actor built a woodworking shop, a chicken coop, and a garden where he grows “strawberries, rhubarb, tomatoes, basil, corn, a beautiful asparagus bed that’s five years old, and watermelon, which is hard to grow up here,” Ruffalo said. “Now I’m doing a little orchard—raspberries, Honeycrisp apples, blueberries, a pear tree.”

In the mid-2010s, Ruffalo moved his primary residence back to NYC for his children’s schooling. “We try to get to our place in Callicoon as much as we can on weekends and holidays and of course spend the summer there,” he said in 2016. “It’s a place I will always hold dear to my heart, filled with lifetime friends and lots of positive sentiment. It’s the best, most-interlocked community I have ever lived in save for my early years in Los Angeles when I was scraping it out to become an actor.” Ruffalo also compared the region to his upbringing in Wisconsin: “Just outside my town there were vast dairy farms, where I would spend my days as a boy fishing in creeks and ponds or climbing around in trees. Everything about the Catskills reminds me of my childhood. I don’t know what to say other than it’s my home.”

Ruffalo and Coigney were married in 2000 and welcomed the first of three children the following year. In December 2004, a few months before their second child was born, the growing family moved into a three-bedroom Hollywood Hills home that they bought for about $1.7 million. It was the cherry on top of a banner year for Ruffalo, who appeared in four movies that year: We Don’t Live Here Anymore, Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, 13 Going on 30, and Collateral.

According to The Los Angeles Times, the gated single-story residence dated to 1933 and was built in the style of a Connecticut farmhouse. Across 3,000 square feet, it hosted three bedrooms, four bathrooms, and a detached guesthouse. Highlights included a fireplace-warmed living room with beamed ceilings, and a breakfast room.

Ruffalo and Coigney welcomed their third child in 2007, then sold the Los Angeles house for $1.65 million two years later to New Girl star Zooey Deschanel and her then husband, Death Cab for Cutie frontman Ben Gibbard. Deschanel and Gibbard divorced in 2012, and Deschanel sold the property in 2015, the Los Angeles Times reported.

Ruffalo’s next real estate purchase was a $3.5 million town house in Brooklyn’s Carroll Gardens neighborhood in 2015. Spanning 3,000 square feet, the 1899-built residence had four bedrooms, three bathrooms, a backyard garden, and dreamy period details: cathedral ceilings, marble fireplaces, decorative arches, and wide-plank wood flooring. There was also a large kitchen with a high-end range, a sunroom with a balcony, and a curved wooden staircase leading to the upstairs bedrooms.

The actor sold the Brooklyn home in 2017 for $3.2 million—a slight loss.

Mark Ruffalo at a rally for the Landmark West Park Presbyterian Church in 2025

Though he left Brooklyn, Ruffalo was not leaving NYC altogether—just moving across the river to Manhattan. In January 2017, he and Coigney were seen touring a $9.99 million six-bedroom town house on the Upper West Side. While it doesn’t appear that they signed that deed, the couple did pick up a home in the neighborhood at some point thereafter. The Poor Things star has been a vocal supporter of upholding the landmark status of the neighborhood’s historic West Park Presbyterian Church since 2023. In December 2025, he said that he lived “a block away from the church.” While the details of this real estate transaction are unknown, Ruffalo’s Upper West Side residence is reportedly an early-20th-century four-story town house.

#4907. On Wants You to Feel Your Softest Ride Yet

The Cloudsurfer 3 is built to make everyday runs feel smooth and effortless, even as the miles add up.

Just because you run doesn’t necessarily mean that you’re up on running shoe innovation. In recent years, there have been notable improvements in propulsion and efficiency, thanks to additions like carbon-fiber plates, smart sensors, and midsoles that promise high energy return. What’s more important than these buzzy words is: How do the shoes feel?

After all, you can have footwear designed by rocket scientists, but if you’re uncomfortable with every step, your run will be a slog, no matter the distance. You want your shoe to make the ride feel soft, which is why the On Cloudsurfer 3 stands out over so many others.

On running shoes have always been distinguished by their trademark hollow pods— the “clouds” that are specifically engineered to help create a softer underfoot experience and give the brand its unmistakable look. In the Cloudsurfer 3, On’s CloudTec Phase™ allows those pods to compress in sequence, helping absorb impact and create a smoother transition from heel to toe. This isn’t just another update to On’s running shoe line. With breakthrough Swiss engineering working beneath every step, the Cloudsurfer 3 delivers the brand’s softest ride yet.

An option for everyday and recovery runs as well as longer training sessions, the Cloudsurfer 3 combines CloudTec® Phase with On’s brand-new SurrealTM Superfoam. According to the brand’s internal testing, the pairing provides 15.5 percent deeper compression—and therefore more impact absorption—than the superfoam alone. The result is a softer landing that can help daily miles feel easier on the legs, particularly over long distances.

According to the same internal testing, the Cloudsurfer 3 is also predicted to deliver a 9.9 percent improvement in smooth-ride sensation. That figure reflects the way the reimagined CloudTec® Phase orientation enhances the rolling motion of the foot, helping each step flow more naturally into the next from landing to toe-off.

You’re also getting a newly engineered mesh upper in the Cloudsurfer 3, which provides a secure fit that adapts to your foot while still offering breathability and support. That breathability helps keep heat and moisture from building up, reducing the conditions that can lead to chafing, blisters, and hot spots.

Even the cushioning around the collar and tongue has been updated, so you get a cloud-like feel as soon as you slip them on. It doesn’t hurt that the Cloudsurfer 3 looks cool, too.

Together, these innovations give runners what they want from an everyday shoe: a natural feel, reliable performance, and lasting comfort. The result is a smoother ride, whether you’re going long or heading out for a quick training run.

That softer feel is a big deal, considering a 2025 study found that runners who perceived their shoes as more cushioned had a lower risk of running-related injury. When a shoe feels right, you’re less likely to think about every step—or adjust the way you’re moving to compensate for discomfort. That allows you to settle into your natural stride and focus on the run itself.

Enjoyment is a major factor, too. Wearing a shoe like the Cloudsurfer 3, with its focus on cushioning, responsiveness, and comfort, can be key to unlocking your best run yet—and enjoying yourself along the way. When that happens, even a hard run can feel softer, mile after mile.

#4906. Volkswagen recalls nearly 73,000 EVs due to faulty batteries

Volkswagen issued a recall affecting nearly 73,000 EVs globally. Until a remedy is available, VW will limit charging on impacted vehicles to 80% of their maximum battery capacity.

After issuing a recall with the NHTSA earlier this month that impacts 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs in the US, official information from the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) reveals several thousand more EVs are affected worldwide.

In three separate recalls now under investigation by the KBA, a total of 72,668 EVs are impacted worldwide, including 9,881 in Germany.

The recall affects certain batches of the ID. Buzz, ID.3, ID.4, and ID.7 models produced between 2022 and 2025, as well as Cupra Born models from 2022 to 2024.

Volkswagen issued the recall after an internal investigation found that some battery cells produced during that period do not meet specifications. The recall stems from a supplier defect.

In some instances, “certain charging profiles combined with a state of charge over 80% may trigger thermal propagation,” or a battery fire, Volkswagen said.

Until a remedy is available, Volkswagen is urging owners to limit charging to 80% of its max capacity. If technically possible, VW said: “the maximum available charging capacity will be temporarily limited to 80% by the system.”

In the US, Volkswagen emailed owners of vehicles included in the recall, saying that unless they opt out by October 21, it “intends to apply a temporary vehicle setting that limits charging to 80%.”

The update will be done remotely and reflected in the mobile app on or about October 27, 2026. Some owners have already received the update.

Sounds like VW's "GM Bolt" moment. Sad. This is a huge cost due to a supplier's failure (but fully understandable and needed), not to mention owners frustration with EVs and the brand.

Volkswagen is still working on a remedy. Letters informing owners of the risks are expected to be mailed out on November 27, 2026. Once the remedy is available, VW will send additional letters.

Owners can contact Volkswagen’s customer service at 1-800-893-5298 with questions or concerns. VW’s recall number is 93EX.

Those in the US can also contact the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration Vehicle Safety Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit NHTSA.gov for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V630.

The manufacturer’s recall codes with the German KBA are 93MV, 93MF, and 93W4 (for the Cupra Born).

#4905. Influencers Are Doing ‘Olive Oil Shots.’ We Asked 4 Experts If That’s a Good Idea—and They All Basically Said the Same Thing.

The truth about the supposed health practice—revealed.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

SO OLIVE OIL shots are a thing again. Remember in the mid- to late-2010s, when people were knocking back all manner of liquids, including apple cider vinegar, juiced ginger, pulverized turmeric, and extra virgin olive oil? Well, social media influencers have brought back at least the last one, with Bryan Johnson doing “evo” shots and Steven Gundry, MD, recommending a daily dose of the stuff. (Also, both those guys sell their own olive oil. Just saying.)

The supposed benefits of shooting olive range from the more generalized “more energy” to more specific ones, like protecting your cardiovascular system from disease.

Influencers usually back up these claims by citing scientific research on the benefits of adding olive oil to your daily diet. But do the benefits extend to doing shots of olive oil?

“Olive oil is great for heart health and contains beneficial polyphenols, but you don't need to take it as a shot. You get the same benefits by just including it in your meals, and it's generally much more enjoyable that way. But if you want to take it as a shot, there's no harm in that. It's just not superior to including olive oil in your diet in regular ways. You know, with food.”

“I'm a fan of California Olive Ranch 100% California Extra Virgin Olive Oil For Everyday. It's high quality, reasonably affordable (for evoo), and widely available. I use it to saute veggies, roast tubers and veggies, and drizzle on various things.”

“I'm a bigger fan of eating a few shots of olive oil with sauteed veggies or I pour it on my food. But a shot is fine I guess. People like to do it in the longevity scene to invoke ancient Greeks doing shots of ‘liquid gold.’”

“I am an affiliate of the Fresh Pressed Olive Oil Club, which I reallly love. I've not had lots of fancy, fresh olive oils from around the world before and now I have. I like seeing and tasting the diversity. I use a 1-liter glass bottle of EVOO, usually Braggs or Whole Food Organic. I try to go through two to three of these a month for our house of four.”

“I wouldn’t suggest shots of olive oil for any reason. All that’s happening here is that you’re adding a concentrated source of calories and fat to your diet. There are no documented benefits of doing this for the average person, and it can cause weight gain if the oil shots are taken in addition to someone’s current diet. This can ultimately cause health problems.”

“I don’t really have a fave oil. I use brands that have a seal of origin in them to ensure their purity.”

“While olive oil is full of beneficial compounds that may support heart health and longevity, shooting it isn't necessary. Heating olive oil may degrade some beneficial polyphenols, but using it as a salad dressing, sauce, or finishing oil for roasted veggies provides the same benefits, plus enhanced absorption of fat-soluble vitamins and carotenoids.”

“Extra-virgin olive oil can have such a range of flavors. I love San Giuliano Coastal Harvest Olive Oil. It's cold-pressed, which helps preserve more nutrients and polyphenols, and has a really nice, peppery flavor. While I don't take shots of it, I regularly use it in dressings and over veggies.”

#4904. 7 Best Lumbar Pillows Bolster Your Back and Bedscape (2026)

Though a lumbar pillow is typically the last detail in making a bed, it’s often the first thing you or a guest will notice. Because it’s long and low, its best suited to the space in front of loftier throw pillows, making a horizon line across your bedscape, and it can bring in a color or texture the rest of the room is vying for. The shape turns up all over AD’s archives, including in supermodel Paloma Elsesser’s Brooklyn home and this classically decorated Southern house.

A lumbar pillow can mean two things: a firm or cushioned gel pillow designed to support the lower back, or an elegant decorative detail among your bedding. While we like both, we’ll leave the Cushion Lab’s best-of for another day. Here, we’re focused on a more inspirational lineup, between linen, wool, velvet, and cotton lumbar pillows that pull a bed and sofa together (and still give your lower back something to lean on in an accent chair). Below are the seven we like best.

Sometimes one pillow is all a bed really needs. West Elm’s oversized linen pillow cover has the scale to anchor a queen or king bed on its own, creating a clean, pulled-together look without a full stack of throw pillows. The linen keeps it loose, making it especially well-suited to coastal, minimalist, modern farmhouse, and casual contemporary spaces.

This pillow is all about texture. Its dimensional surface gives a sofa or bed a more layered, considered look without relying on a loud print or saturated color. In other words, its style will speak volumes even when paired with quieter neutrals.

At 48 inches, Quince’s velvet lumbar is long enough to span a queen bed with nothing else in front of it, and the cotton pile catches light in a way linen won’t. The glacier blue reads cool and a little silvery against white or oatmeal bedding. It’s dry clean only, and the insert is sold separately.

Color is the point with this Athena cushion. Rather than fading quietly into the background, this lumbar pillow is designed to bring energy to a room, whether it’s breaking up the monotony of a neutral living room or adding contrast to a more restrained bedding scheme. It’s the kind of accent that makes a pillow arrangement feel more collected, playful, and intentional.

A little color can go a long way, especially in the form of Pendleton’s Turquoise Crosses Lumbar Pillow. Its vivid palette and geometric pattern give neutral furniture or a plain accent chair an instant lift. For anyone drawn to Southwestern-inspired textiles, this pick brings just enough graphic punch without crowding the rest of the room.

The Mendocino cover is made up of hand-dyed washed linen, so the color shifts slightly across the surface instead of sitting flat. What separates it from the other linen picks here is the fringe: three-inch knotted tassels run along two sides, which give a simple lumbar some movement at the ends of a sofa or bed. Nota bene: the insert is sold separately.

Washed linen has a way of making a room feel more relaxed and breezy, which is exactly the appeal of Brooklinen’s pillow cover. The simple design is easy to fold into an existing pillow arrangement, while the softly textured fabric and choice of vibrant hues keep it from feeling too plain.

A lumbar pillow is a long, rectangular cushion designed to support the lower back. The term describes two different products: one is the ergonomic back support pillow, often memory foam, made for an office chair or car seat. The other is the decorative version on this list, which works as an accent piece on beds, sofas, benches, and accent chairs. Their shape makes them especially useful for layering with standard square throw pillows, adding dimension without making a space feel cluttered.

One of the easiest ways to style a lumbar pillow is to place it in front of larger pillows or shams on a bed. On a sofa or accent chair, a lumbar pillow can serve as a single focal point or be paired with smaller throw pillows in complementary colors, patterns, or textures. For a more polished look, choose a lumbar pillow that either picks up a color already in the room or brings in a contrasting texture, like linen, wool, velvet, or tassels.

For lower back support, a lumbar pillow goes in the curve between your back and the back of a sofa, reading chair, or recliner chair. Keep in mind a firmer, fuller back pillow will likely do more for your posture than a soft, decorative one. For styling, it can also be centered across a bed, layered in front of sleeping pillows, or placed on a bench for extra comfort and visual interest. Oversized lumbar pillows work especially well on queen and king beds because they can anchor the entire pillow arrangement with one clean horizontal line.

#4903. Lexus announces prices for its first 3-row electric SUV in Europe and the US

Lexus announced prices for its first fully electric three-row SUV, the 2027 TZ, with sales set to begin in the US later this year and in Europe in early 2027.

The new TZ is the largest, most luxurious Lexus electric SUV to date. It will go on sale by the end of 2026 in the US, and early 2027 in Europe.

In the US, the 2027 Lexus TZ will be available in three trims, starting at $64,050. The base TZ 450e Premium AWD model will be available to order in late 2026, followed by the Premium Touring AWD and Luxury AWD trims in early 2027.

The three-row electric SUV will be available with two battery packs: 76.96 kWh and 95.82 kWh. The former provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 253 miles, while the latter gets up to 315 miles.

All TZ variants come with an evolved version of Lexus’ DIRECT4 AWD system. The dual-motor AWD setup delivers a combined 308 horsepower.

Inside, the three-row electric SUV features the latest Lexus Interface multimedia system. The setup includes a 14″ multimedia touchscreen display with customizable widgets, a Voice Assistant, and full-screen navigation on the digital cluster.

The 2027 Lexus TZ is 200.8″ long, 78.3″ wide, and 67.1″ tall, with a 120.1″ wheelbase, or roughly the same size as the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and the Volvo EX90.

The base 2027 Lexus TZ 450e Premium AWD will be available to order later this year, starting at $64,050 with up to 253 miles of range.

In early 2027, the Touring and Luxury models will go on sale, starting at $72,050 and $80,550, respectively. Both use the extended-range 95.82 kWh battery. The Touring model offers up to 315 miles of range, while the most expensive Luxury trim gets 279 miles.

Lexus said the electric SUV can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 35 minutes at up to 150 kW. It also includes an NACS charge port so you can access Tesla Superchargers without a separate adapter.

Lexus revealed TZ prices in several European markets ahead of its official market launch in early 2027.

I have to admit that first pic (blue one) looks pretty nice for an SUV. But not so great when you get to that interior.

I'm looking forward to the day when manufacturers start building the screens back into the dash more instead of this awful Tesla-like screen stuck to the dash look.

In the Netherlands, it will be available in three variants: 450e Standard Range, 450e Long Range Executive Line, and 450e Long Range President Line.

The base Standard Range model starts at 79,995 euros ($90,000), including a limited-time 4,000 euro discount.

It uses the same 77 kWh and 95.8 kWh batteries, offering a WLTP range of up to 280 miles (450 km) and 338 miles (544 km), respectively.

In Spain, the 2027 Lexus TZ will go on sale starting at 88,000 euros ($99,000), with prices ranging up to 105,000 euros ($118,000) for the top-spec Luxury two-tone variant.

#4902. The 16 Best Men's Clothing Brands in 2026, According to Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

From the OG classics to newcomer labels you need to know.

AS MEN’S HEALTH EDITORS, we give guys tools they need to level up their lives, and that includes your wardrobe. Enter: The best men's clothing brands for men, a shortlist of labels that deliver on style and function for every vibe and occasion. Whether you’re a seasoned fashion maven or just dipping your toes into the menswear game, having a solid rotation of duds you can rely on is key to looking sharp without overthinking it. More importantly, the right brands make it easy, whether you need office-ready staples, weekend essentials, or something that’ll turn heads on a night out, you can rest assured that you’re getting the same fit every time from the same brand.

Since 2020, our style editors have tested more than 80 clothing brands for men, exploring all kinds of styles including activewear, business casual, sharp tailoring, outerwear layers, and everything in between. To curate the best of the best, we focused on three things: Clothes that are built to last, look sharp, and make you feel unstoppable. Below, the 16 best men's clothing brands that nail craftsmanship, timeless style, and all-around wearability.

Huckberry's in-house label delivers a rugged, workwear-inspired vibe, made with utility and style in mind. Flint & Tinder is essentially for the guy who wants clothes that feel cool and work as hard as he does. The pieces aren’t just about looking good; they can handle all kinds of weather, provide comfort, and won’t fray at the end of a few wears. You get authentic American workwear aesthetics with modern details, meaning every piece can handle everyday wear and the occasional adventure.

In terms of selects, the lineup is super versatile. Expect quality, uniform staples; think robust flannels, durable outerwear (like waxed canvas jackets), sturdy chinos, and comfortable, well-constructed basics. Whether you’re going on a camping trip, chopping down some wood, or grabbing beers with your pals, these designs make for excellent gear in the city, in the wild, and beyond.

If we had to choose one of our favorites from F&T, it would be the Flannel-Lined Waxed Trucker Jacket that looks burly on the outside but feels super toasty on the inside. When the weather breaks, it does a bang-up job at keeping the rain, wind, and cold temps at bay.

Read More: Best Clothing Subscription Boxes for Men

With a roster of products that spans everything from T-shirts and underwear to activewear, Mack Weldon builds a complete wardrobe that’s both high-performing and versatile for your everyday life. In using a variety of innovative fabrics and technologies, the brand offers clothes that look great, feel incredible, and are engineered to withstand your weekly routine (i.e. long work days, rigorous HIIT sessions, all-day errand runs).

If you’re a busy body and constantly on the move, you can find a number of items to support your active lifestyle. In fact, performance features like moisture-wicking and anti-odor protection make it easy to transition from the gym to your daily grind without missing a beat. As for casual outings, Mack Weldon has you covered in that area, too. Whether that means baseball games, coffee dates, or happy hour meet-ups, the clean, minimal designs are a great fit for a polished yet relaxed look, too.

Speaking of which, the Ace Sweatpant is a total winner. Made with micro-brushed French terry, it’s a pair that offers a flattering fit, plenty of breathability, and won’t make you look out of place, no matter where you are.

Read More: Mack Weldon Airknitx Boxer Brief Review

Abercrombie used to be one of those mall-favorites back in the day, but the brand has since revamped its all-American cool–think easygoing duds, with a hint of vintage flair. Its range of versatile, premium-feeling designs are mostly laid-back and look great on guys of all ages. These threads work perfectly in casual environments where you want to look put-together but leave the high maintenance at home. At its core, the brand is all about comfort that doesn’t sacrifice style.

Whether you’re attending a music festival, cruising downtown with friends, or hitting up a weekend bonfire, you can find pieces that transition from day to night, making sure you’re always on point—no matter the occasion. Abercrombie specializes in those casual staples that you need in rotation such as cozy hoodies, sleek vegan leather jackets, perfectly worn-in t-shirts, and several types of denim cuts. When it comes to the latter, the 90s Straight Jean has been a huge hit, offering a wide selection of washes, plenty of stretch, and retro charm.

Bonobos got its start because the founders were fed up with pants that just didn’t cut it. With universal fits at its heart, they set out to build wardrobe essentials that actually work for every guy, no matter his build. Instead of sticking with small, medium, and large sizes, the brand’s assortment of pants features over 12 different waist sizes, plus a range of inseams and fits including athletic, slim taper, and straight. This means you’re guaranteed to find the perfect pair. In tandem with the selection of pants, the shirts come in a series of fits, too.

Aside from killer chinos, the vast inventory consists of golf gear, suits and blazers, swim trunks, and outerwear. In fact, it was the relaxed cut of The Harrington Jacket that resonated with us, which layers easily over all kinds of tops. All things considered, if you need new attire for the beach, the links, the office, or the weekend, it’s all here.

If you've never heard of Buck Mason, think of this LA-based brand as a one-stop-shop for guys who want to look put-together but not pretentious. Instead of chasing trends, the label is set on offering a refined take on everyday essentials, blending American style with modern tailoring and quality craftsmanship. In other words, its expertise lies in paying attention to the details: Taking into account fabric, fit, and function. After all, the brand acquired an American knitting mill to ensure its gear stays authentically made in the USA. As a result, this men’s clothing brand’s designs are about that understated style with classic silhouettes and muted color palettes, mixed with a twist of laid-back California vibes.

Falling in line with those aesthetics is its best-selling, signature Felted Chore Coat—simple at first glance, but crafted with purpose. We love that it's tailored with a slimmer cut through the arms for a sharper silhouette, while the roomier torso leaves space for layering. Plus, the felted merino wool allows you to capitalize on warmth, breathability, and softness without bulk.

In general, Buck Mason’s pieces work in a variety of settings—be it a dinner date, food festival, or Broadway show. Among its collection of garments is high-quality jeans, t-shirts and henleys, button-down shirts and lightweight jackets.

Todd Snyder is known for modernizing classic American menswear with tailored fits, top-of-the-line fabrics, and subtle yet stylish updates. The brand blends timeless silhouettes with contemporary details, often playing with rich textures and unique color palettes. While Todd Snyder is not exactly budget-friendly, the slew of suede jackets, wool coats, and refined suiting will let you channel the best A-listers in the game. In fact, its vintage-inspired sweaters and outerwear have even graced the likes of Chris Evans and Ryan Reynolds.

An undeniable standout is the Italian Suede Snap Dylan Jacket that’s structured enough to look sharp but accommodate easy layering. The trucker-style cut is crafted from buttery-soft calf suede, which not only gives luxury feels but also ages beautifully over time.

Another one of Todd Snyder's biggest strengths is its collaborations, from Timex watches to New Balance sneakers and Champion heritage sweatpants. These partnerships add a level of flair that few brands are able to mimic. Overall, TS expertly delivers high-quality, long-lasting staples that work for guys who want to look put-together without trying too hard.

Everlane is a men's clothing brand that follows its own path. It's really big on creating eco-conscious, classic clothes that will cycle through your ever-evolving wardrobe for years to come. Think authentic denim and minimal organic cotton tees priced so well that you won't have any other option than to stock up on multiple pairs and colorways.

If you're looking to stay cozy through the last stretch of winter, Everlane's got a whole Cashmere Shop filled with ultra-soft sweaters to keep you warm without overheating. The brand’s assortment also makes it easy to transition from the office to happy hour with its monochromatic shirting—from oxford shirts to shackets such as the versatile Heavyweight Overshirt—that has that just-right fit that's neither too slim nor too boxy.

Perhaps best known in the zeitgeist for its finance bro vests, Patagonia is in fact the leading outdoor apparel brand that makes clothes with adventures and extreme climates in mind. It has tons of hiking-inspired basics to anchor a stylish and functional closet. For starters, The Nano Puff Jacket is the gold standard of puffer jackets—light, warm, and endlessly versatile—ideal for street and trail wear. Not to mention, it's a warrior in all kinds of weather, thanks to the windproof and water-repellent exterior.

Its fleece layers are legendary, too. Take the Better Sweater Fleece Jacket, which is cozy, durable, and polished enough to wear just about anywhere. This silhouette is thicker than a standard fleece, but the regular fit allows you to layer effortlessly. In terms of style, you can wear it for weekend hikes or the nearest coffee shop for your daily pick-me-up.

This stalwart label has been in the game for ages and still gets it right—serving up sleek clothing for men, which embodies "quiet luxury" energy, minus the high-roller price tag. When it comes to styling Banana Republic, picture yourself nailing every look—from acing that morning meeting in a crisp dress shirt and tailored chinos, to seamlessly transitioning into dinner at a swanky bistro with a smart blazer.

The brand’s offerings are built for real life, so whether you’re powering through a busy workday, networking at after-hours events, or catching up with friends over drinks on the weekend, there’s something to fit the bill. Banana Republic specializes in dressier, well-cut staples: Sharp button-downs, versatile trousers, structured blazers, and quality knitwear that feels as good as it looks. But make no mistake, Banana Republic also plays with casual attire too. For example, the Ribbed Cotton Henley T-Shirt has that relaxed feel, which is great for those off-duty days when you’re picking up lunch or taking a laid-back stroll in the park.

Alex Mill’s been around for over a decade, carving out a reputation we’d describe as “Normcore classic.” In other words, the brand hits it on the nail when it comes to everyday basics—think slub tees that serve as the ultimate wardrobe workhorses, slightly cropped jeans that pair with any top, and washed chore coats that add dimension to any look. It’s all about minimal fuss, modern sensibility, and letting the pieces become more character-rich with every wear.

These garments really come into their own in spots like creative offices, co-working spaces, or that favorite local cafe—places where you want to look put-together without trying too hard. They’re perfect for laid-back brunches, art gallery openings, or casual dinner dates. Without seeming overdone, these staples can easily elevate your everyday style. Take the Garment Dyed Chore Jacket in Canvas, for instance: It's super low-key—not too in your face, yet still has that unique twist that any artist or designer would appreciate.

The Japanese brand helped redefine what great wardrobe essentials should feel like: clean, well-made, and affordable without ever looking cheap. Its lineup is built around minimal design and great-for-the-price fabrics (think Heattech thermals, a heat-retaining base layer designed to trap warmth without bulk, or Ultra Light Down, Uniqlo’s featherweight yet surprisingly warm down insulation), offering pieces that work across seasons—from crisp tees and chinos to cozy sweaters and functional outerwear that earns its closet space.

What makes Uniqlo a go-to is its ability to effortlessly fit into everyday life. These are clothes you grab on busy workdays, for travel, or just when you want to get dressed without overthinking it. Whether you’re layering thermals under a jacket for winter or reaching for a casual linen in the summer, Uniqlo’s pieces are the building blocks that make everything else in your wardrobe work better.

J.Crew is one of those heritage American labels that you often circle back to because it just gets the classics right. The brand is known for its preppy-meets-laid-back aesthetic, offering staples like blazers, button-downs, chinos, knitwear, and polos that feel polished but never stuffy.These are the kinds of pieces that carry you through a full day from the office to post-work drinks without needing an outfit change. If your style lives somewhere between casual and pulled-together, J.Crew makes it easy to look sharp in a way that feels chill and approachable at the same time.

Cos is the more elevated sibling to H&M—part of the same family, but built around higher-quality fabrics and more refined construction. Rather than chasing trends, Cos invests in premium wool blends, heavyweight cottons, and structured tailoring, which its pieces cost a bit more than its sister brand, but also hold their shape and look polished far longer. You’re paying for better fabric, cleaner finishing, and silhouettes that don’t feel disposable. Its lineup includes sharp wool overcoats, crisp poplin button-downs, substantial merino knits, and tailored trousers with a proper drape—all in shades like black, navy, charcoal, or stone. These clothes can transition from the office to a fancy dinner to speakeasy nightcap situation. Essentially, this is where you go for something a step above fast fashion minus the designer price tag.

Alo may have started as an active brand, but it’s evolved into a full-on lifestyle label that blends workout clothes with fits that you’d wear outside the gym. From moisture-wicking workout tees and sleek tanks to comfortable hoodies and joggers that look good in public, these are the pieces you throw on for a morning session, keep on for errands, travel days, or a casual lunch, and still feel clean.

Tailored cargo trousers, straight-leg Velour pants, and track pants with clean hems and minimal branding can pass at the office, while the carpenter-style bottoms and relaxed cargos feel polished enough for dinner plans. Up top, Alo’s bombers, pullover sweatshirts, and shackets are structured, not slouchy or logo-heavy, making them easy substitutes for a crewneck, knit, or light jacket.

If your uniform leans athletic but put-together, without looking like you just walked out of a sweat-drenched Barry’s class, Alo makes it easy to never feel under- or overdressed. One note: most of its clothing runs big, so be sure to size down for a closer fit, unless you prefer a looser cut.

Madewell established its reputation on solid denim, and that foundation still shows, but over the years the brand has evolved beyond jeans. Over the past few years, it’s quietly strengthened its menswear roster, offering easy essentials like soft tees, cozy knits, overshirts, and brushed flannels that layer cleanly without bunching. The overall vibe at Madewell is relaxed but put-together. These clothes are made for weekends, casual dinners, and low-key nights at a bar or speakeasy. They feel broken-in from day one but still read sharp. If your uniform starts with great denim and goes from there, Madewell is an excellent place to begin.

Few brands have done more to define American prep than Tommy Hilfiger. From rugby shirts and flag sweaters to chinos, polos, and lightweight outerwear, the label consistently delivers timeless staples that feel both classic and current. What keeps Tommy relevant, though, is its knack for evolving the formula through smart collaborations and fresh takes on heritage style. Recent partnerships, including its ongoing work with the U.S. SailGP Team, prove the brand still knows how to make prep feel cool for a new generation.

A polished but relaxed approach to office dressing that’s also suitable for after-work drinks—think chinos, dress shirts, knit polos, and unstructured blazers. Brands such as Bonobos, Alex Mill, and Banana Republic have this kind of style down pat.

If you have plans to attend a black-tie event, gala, wedding, or simply want to look extra sharp, you’ve got to suit up. In this case, you’ll turn to structured blazers, tailored trousers, dress shirts, and dress shoes in classic colors like navy, gray, and black. Brands such as Bonobos, Todd Snyder, Banana Republic, and Buck Mason have suiting on lock.

From lightweight jackets to heavy-duty coats, outerwear is all about function and style. This includes bombers, leather jackets, shackets, parkas, and puffers perfect for transitional weather or full-on winter. Brands such as Flint and Tinder, Patagonia, and Alex Mill will have you geared up.

Clothing designed for movement but stylish enough for everyday wear. Think workout shirts, joggers, sweat-wicking polos, gym shorts, and sneakers that work for both gym sessions and casual outings. Brands like Alo and Patagonia offer a solid collection of these duds.

Easygoing staples like jeans, hoodies, henleys, sneakers, and flannels—perfect for relaxed weekends, brunch, or laid-back office days. Brands such as Abercrombie, J.Crew, Everlane, and Uniqlo deliver in this category.

When shopping for the best clothing brands for men, fit is everything. It dictates not only how comfortable you feel but also how your outfit communicates your personal style. Generally, men’s garments are broken down into four broad categories: Relaxed, Tailored, Classic, and Slim. You don’t have to stick to just one, but each serves a different aesthetic and function—let’s break it down.

Relaxed-fit clothing is all about comfort. It’s cut with extra room through the chest, waist, and legs, allowing for a looser, more laid-back silhouette. This is ideal if you’re looking for casual wear, streetwear, and workwear-inspired looks. Think boxy tees, oversized hoodies, wide-leg trousers, and unstructured outerwear. Patagonia tends to lean into this fit as its fleece jackets, outerwear, and casual basics are built for movement and outdoor adventure. Alex Mill focuses on casual staples with slightly relaxed, vintage-inspired cuts.

A tailored fit offers a balance between structure and comfort. It follows the body’s shape without clinging too tightly, creating a refined yet wearable look. This is your go-to fit for business casual, smart casual, and elevated everyday wear. Think tapered chinos, slightly structured blazers, and slim-but-not-skinny button-downs.

Slim fits are designed for a clean, modern silhouette. These clothes contour the body without excessive looseness, making them ideal for dressier looks, contemporary minimalism, or even athleisure. Key pieces include slim-fit jeans, fitted turtlenecks, and sharply cut blazers.

Classic fit is the middle ground between relaxed and tailored, giving you room to move without excess fabric. This is the fit you’ll find in traditional menswear, from business suits to heritage denim. It’s not baggy, but it’s also not hugging your body either.

Not all clothes are created equal, and neither are price tags. Some items are worth dropping some serious cash on, while others can be a rip-off. The key is knowing when to invest and when to save because a well-thought-out wardrobe isn’t about spending the most, it’s about getting the most value out of what you buy.

This is your fast-fashion and essentials tier—solid for trying new styles or grabbing wardrobe basics without overthinking. But here’s the catch: Cheap can often mean short-lived. For instance, a $10 tee from a fast-fashion retailer may look good today but will likely warp, fade, or pill after a few washes. That’s fine for trends like an oversized striped tee you might wear for a season, but when it comes to daily staples, spending a little more pays off. You’d be better off spending $58 on an Alex Mill slub tee that lasts for years and is worn 50-plus times, which equals less than $2 per wear.

This is where cost meets quality. You’re getting better fabrics, stronger construction, and brands that care about longevity. Think nicer denim, well-cut chinos, and quality knitwear—things you’ll actually wear often, so the investment makes sense.

This is where justifiable spending comes into play. A $500 Buck Mason suede jacket? Pricey up front, but wear it 50 times per season for five years, and suddenly, it’s $2 per wear—less than a daily coffee. The same goes for boots—drop $300+ on a well-made pair, and you won’t have to replace them for a decade. In this price range, you find premium outerwear, leather goods, boots, and everyday pieces.

At this level, you’re paying for craftsmanship, exclusivity, and long-term investment. A $1,300 leather jacket from Todd Snyder isn’t for everyone, but if you’re buying into history, durability, and premium construction, it’ll outlive you. Same with a properly tailored suit—if you wear it for major life events over decades, it’s an investment, not an expense.

To find the best men's clothing brands, our fashion and commerce teams, led by Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, spent the last five years putting over 80 menswear brands through the wringer, wearing threads to sweaty gym sessions, breezy hikes, long workdays, formal cocktail events, and casual weekend outings. Whether it was testing a fleece in the cold, seeing if dress shirts hold up in marathon meetings, or figuring out if chinos had enough stretch for comfort during a long-haul flight, we made sure these brands actually delivered on function as well as style.

From there, we narrowed it down to 16 standout brands based on quality, fit, signature styles, type of garment, and value. No fast fashion, no fleeting trends, just well-made, great-fitting essentials that look sharp on any guy, hold up over time, and feel like a solid investment for our wardrobe. #4901. Lucid’s 25,000 Bolt robotaxis will run on Nvidia’s self-driving software

Lucid’s European robotaxi deal now has a driver. Bolt announced today that its fleet of at least 25,000 autonomous Lucid vehicles will run Nvidia’s Alpamayo Stack self-driving software, starting with a data-collection program in Madrid in 2027.

That gives Lucid two robotaxi customers on two different autonomy systems: Nuro’s software for Uber’s Gravity robotaxis in the US, and now Nvidia’s for Bolt in Europe.

When Lucid and Bolt announced the 25,000-vehicle deal last month, nobody said who would write the driving software. The vehicles were to be built around Nvidia Hyperion, a reference design for compute and sensors, which isn’t a self-driving system on its own. Bolt said it would bring in autonomous-driving partners later.

It picked Nvidia again. Alpamayo Stack is Nvidia’s full-stack driving software, which the company describes as “reasoning AI” combined with classical perception and planning, running on Hyperion with its Halos safety tools on top. The two will tune the software for European driving, and Lucid is only the first automaker Bolt plans to put it in.

Madrid comes first, in 2027. The cars there won’t carry riders at the start. Their job is to collect real-world driving data so Bolt and Nvidia can develop and validate the software, and even that still needs regulatory approval. Germany and France are named as the next key markets.

Jevgeni Kabanov, Bolt’s president and head of autonomous driving, said the Region of Madrid is “pioneering a structured framework for commercial autonomous mobility.” On Lucid’s side, the work runs through Lucid Technologies. Its president, Kay Stepper, called the “launch of data collection next year” one of “the first steps” toward autonomous mobility in Europe.

Bolt didn’t say which Lucid model goes to Madrid.

The September deal was designed around Lucid’s upcoming Midsize platform, the same platform whose first vehicle, the Cosmos, got pushed to 2027 in Lucid’s August operating reset, “most likely the second half.” If the purpose-built vehicle isn’t ready in time, Madrid’s first data-collection cars would have to be existing Gravity or Air vehicles.

There’s also no date for anyone riding without a driver. Data collection is step one.

Add up both programs and Lucid has a lot of robotaxis on order, at least on paper. Uber’s program with Lucid and Nuro now calls for at least 35,000 Gravity vehicles globally, up from Uber’s original commitment to 20,000. Bolt adds at least 25,000. That’s 60,000 vehicles.

For scale, Lucid delivered 15,841 vehicles in all of 2025 and 10,852 in the first nine months of 2026. Those robotaxi commitments equal almost four years of Lucid’s current deliveries.

So Bolt is a company, with the same name as the Chevy Bolt. That makes the headline look a little confusing.

The Uber program is further along, but it isn’t open to the public yet. Uber employees have been taking test rides in Gravity robotaxis in San Francisco since April, with a safety operator behind the wheel. The public Bay Area launch is still promised for 2026, with Houston to follow in mid-2027.

Bolt is also hedging. It runs a separate track with Pony.ai and Stellantis, which announced a pilot in Luxembourg in June, and it’s targeting 100,000 autonomous vehicles on its platform across Europe and the wider UNECE region by 2035.

As for Nvidia, it has spent years selling chips and sensor reference designs to automakers. With Alpamayo Stack, it’s now selling the driver too, which puts it up against Nuro, Waymo, and Tesla’s software.
